_doc: Canonical stage list for the talking-video world: one or more recordings of someone speaking to camera -> one edited, captioned video. There is no short/long switch — the output orientation follows the source (render_data.py reads it), and every stage runs for both. Read by scripts/run.py; mirrors SKILL.md steps 3-13. `run` is the argv to spawn (cwd = skill dir), with {work} {source} {language} {skill} {ffmpeg} {ffprobe} substituted ({ffmpeg}/{ffprobe} resolve via lib/platform.py - $VEVO_FFMPEG / $VEVO_FFPROBE else PATH). A stage with no `run` is a checkpoint: `block:true` halts run.py until `makes` exists (a genuine human decision); a checkpoint with no `makes` is advisory - printed once, never blocks. A stage runs when any `makes` path is missing or older than any `needs` path; else it is skipped. `needs`/`makes` are work-relative; a trailing / means 'non-empty directory'; a `makes` of `timeline.json#checkpoints.<id>` means content, not a file — true only once `mark_checkpoint.py <work> <id>` marked that decision step addressed. `when` gates a stage on a project.config.json value. The montage lives in one file, <work>/timeline.json, and the human steps edit THAT file rather than each producing one of their own — transcript-fix, cut-review, tighten, chapters, scenes and sound-cues all block on their own `checkpoints` mark this way.

stages.title: Prepare the source (join the takes, tag bt709)
stages.note: Stream copy, never a re-encode: the take(s) concatenated and re-tagged bt709. This one file is what the Remotion render reads directly, cutting it at each segment's `source` — there is no intermediate cut video.

stages.title: Measure the silences
stages.note: A measurement, not a decision: where the speaker is quiet, in source seconds. Nothing ever edits it, so it cannot disagree with the montage. `cut.noiseDb` / `cut.minSilence` shape it; the padding and merging are applied later, by build_timeline.py.

stages.title: Transcribe with per-word timing
stages.note: The second measurement. Like build/silences.json it is never edited — corrections go into timeline.json, so this stays the thing the montage can always be rebuilt from.

stages.title: Build the timeline - one segment per sentence
stages.note: Crosses the two measurements into <work>/timeline.json: one segment per spoken sentence, each carrying the source ranges kept for it and its text — words are never stored, only computed on demand from `text` — and later its scene, its sound cues and its layout. From here on this file IS the montage. It REFUSES to overwrite itself without --force, because rebuilding discards every cut, correction and scene in it.

stages.title: Nudge each cut-in onto a clean frame
stages.note: Nudges each segment's cut-in onto a sharp, settled frame — audio silence alone cannot tell that the speaker is still moving. Config: `cut.settle=false` skips it. Safe to re-run: a cut-in already on a good frame is left alone, and after a tighten pass there are new ones worth settling.

stages.title: Correct the transcript (Claude, whole pass)
stages.note: Claude re-reads the WHOLE transcript in timeline.json. Every incoherent / garbled sentence: recover what was said, else reword it correctly in the video's own language and register (darija stays darija). Edit that segment's `text` directly — `*word*` marks a hot word — and nothing else: word timings are computed fresh from `text` every time they are read (lib/timeline.words()), so there is no separate re-spacing step and nothing to keep in sync. Not a line-by-line session with the user — show a summary. See SKILL.md step 5. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> transcript-fix`.

stages.title: Finalize the script - repeats gone, then your edits
stages.note: Claude reads timeline.json itself, finds every repeated/abandoned attempt at the same idea (keeping the LAST one as the real source) and switches those segments off: `"on": false, "why": "..."` — by hand, or `uv run scripts/cut_entries.py <work> drop 7 12 --why "..."` (by LINE NUMBER — there are no ids; `show` prints the current numbering). `cut_entries.py <work> dupes` reports look-alike neighbours but never decides. Genuinely unsure about a passage -> ask the user, with the line numbers and both texts, don't guess. THEN `cut_entries.py <work> show`, show the numbered script, and cut any whole sentence the creator asks for. Recap what was auto-removed AFTER, not before. Nothing to cut -> continue, still a valid outcome. This can happen in any order relative to scene design: a cut shifts nothing (a `split` does — re-run `show` after one). See SKILL.md step 6. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> cut-review`.

stages.title: Jump-cut + filler pass
stages.note: `uv run scripts/tighten.py <work>` proposes word-level cuts (silences over `tighten.pauseMs`, fillers from scripts/fillers.json); show the summary and the filler list, then `tighten.py <work> apply`. Safe to re-run — it measures the current timeline, so a second apply finds nothing left over the threshold. Nothing over the threshold -> that's a valid outcome too. See SKILL.md step 7. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> tighten`.

stages.title: Chapter markers
stages.note: Only worth proposing on a long recording. Propose 3-8, and after the user confirms give the segment where each one starts a `"chapter": "..."` field, directly in timeline.json — the segment itself is the anchor, so cutting a sentence elsewhere can never move or drop one. Too short for chapters -> that's a valid outcome too. See SKILL.md step 8. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> chapters`.

stages.title: Measure the face framing
stages.note: A measurement, not a decision: where the speaker's face is across the whole recording, in source-frame fractions. Nothing ever edits it. render_data.py turns it into a per-piece zoom/anchor aimed at the active layout's own face target; a segment's own hand-set `zoom`/`anchor` overrides it outright. See SKILL.md step 9.

stages.title: Design the scenes
stages.note: The core creative step. Give an entry a `scene` ({type, params, at, dur}, `at`/`dur` relative to that entry) and a `video.layout`, optionally a `video.filter` and a `video.in` transition, or an `overlay` for a logo/badge on the video itself. Every keyword and parameter is read from the option files, never written from memory: layouts, transitions, scenes and filters are the files of `scripts/remotion/template/src/<domain>/`. A scenes-less project renders with captions only — that is a valid choice, not a skip. See SKILL.md step 10. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> scenes`.

stages.title: Place the sound cues
stages.note: Give the segments that want one an `sfx` list: ["WHOOSH_UP"] — always plays at the segment's own start, so the cue stays glued to its sentence (a cue mid-sentence means splitting the sentence there first: `cut_entries.py split`). The cues are the files of `scripts/sounds/` (UPPERCASE keywords), never written from memory. Set `outro.seconds` for the end card. Keep it under ~15 events/min (rule #1). No cues wanted -> that's a valid outcome too. See SKILL.md step 11. Then: `uv run scripts/mark_checkpoint.py <work> sound-cues`.
